claims.text: A bitmapped image is divided into a grid of pixels, and the file stores a binary colour code for each pixel.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A bitmap file carries a header holding the data needed to read the image, such as the image resolution, the colour depth, the file size and where the pixel data starts.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Image resolution is the number of pixels in the stored image, width by height; screen resolution is the number of pixels the display shows; colour depth (bit depth) is the number of bits stored per pixel.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The pixel data size of a bitmapped image is estimated as the number of pixels multiplied by the colour depth in bits per pixel, plus the small header.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A file size in bits is converted to bytes by dividing by 8, and prefixes are applied to bytes, never to bits.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Raising the colour depth increases the number of colours available, because the count of colour codes is two to the power of the depth, and it increases the file size because each pixel stores more bits.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Raising the image resolution increases the number of pixels describing the scene, so the picture stays sharp at larger sizes and the file size grows with the pixel count.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The image file stores the image resolution, so the screen resolution of the display it is opened on changes how large the picture appears, not one bit of the file.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A vector graphic is stored as a drawing list of drawing objects, and each drawing object is a command with properties, such as its shape, position, size and line or fill colour.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The software displays a vector graphic by working down the drawing list and drawing each object from its properties, so the picture can be drawn at any size.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A bitmap suits a photograph, because its continuous and irregular tones need a colour code for each pixel.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A vector graphic suits a logo or line drawing, because a few objects with properties describe it, the file stays small and the picture redraws sharp at any size, whereas a bitmap loses sharpness when enlarged far past its resolution.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A vector file is typically smaller than a bitmap of the same simple drawing, because the list stores a few commands with properties rather than a code for every pixel.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Sound is analogue, so it is stored by sampling: the wave's amplitude is measured at regular intervals and each measurement is stored as a binary value.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Sampling rate is the number of samples taken per second, measured in hertz, and sampling resolution is the number of bits stored per sample.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A higher sampling rate captures more of the wave's changes each second, so the rebuilt sound is truer, and the file grows because more samples are stored per second.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A higher sampling resolution stores each measurement more precisely, so the rebuilt amplitude is closer to the wave, and the file grows because each sample takes more bits.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
